# StickOut

> Free Online VLSI Stick Diagram, CMOS Diagram, and VLSI Floor Planning Editor.

StickOut is a specialized web-based Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tool designed for electrical & computer engineering students, IC layout designers, and academic researchers. It allows users to quickly draw, analyze, and export publication-ready VLSI stick diagrams, CMOS logic gate circuit schematics, and IC floor plans directly in the browser with zero installation.

## Core Features & Capabilities

- **VLSI Stick Diagram Editor**: Draw interactive stick diagrams with standard IC manufacturing layers including Polysilicon, Metal 1, Metal 2, N-Diffusion, P-Diffusion, N-Well, P-Well, contacts, and vias.
- **CMOS Circuit Diagram Editor**: Place PMOS & NMOS transistor symbols, connection dots, supply rails (VCC/GND), and automatically generate full CMOS gate layouts from Boolean expressions (e.g. `~(A & B)` for NAND, `~(A | B)` for NOR, XOR, AOI, OAI gates).
- **VLSI Floor Planning Tool**: Define top-level chip boundaries, layout functional macro blocks, place input/output/power pin terminals, route power ring wires, and inspect chip area metrics.
- **Automated Jump Detection**: Automatically renders wire crossover jumps when same-layer conductors cross without a contact junction.
- **High-Resolution Export**: Export vector-quality high-resolution PNG images with customizable transparent, light, or dark backgrounds suitable for IEEE/academic papers and presentations.
- **Project Files**: Save and reload projects locally as `.stk` files or autosave in browser local storage.

## Routes & Interactive Pages

- [/](https://stickout.vercel.app/): Main landing page with feature breakdowns, live interactive canvas preview, layer documentation, and tool launching.
- [/stick-diagram](https://stickout.vercel.app/stick-diagram): Standalone VLSI Stick Diagram layout editor interface.
- [/cmos-diagram](https://stickout.vercel.app/cmos-diagram): CMOS schematic and transistor layout editor interface.
- [/floor-planning](https://stickout.vercel.app/floor-planning): VLSI top-level chip floor planning and block placement interface.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

- `V`: Select / Move tool
- `W`: Wire / Line tool
- `Q`: Rectangle / Block tool
- `R`: Rotate selected element (90°)
- `P`: PMOS Transistor (CMOS mode) / Contact tool (Stick mode)
- `N`: NMOS Transistor (CMOS mode)
- `D`: Connection Dot (CMOS mode)
- `L` / `T`: Text Label tool
- `E`: Eraser tool
- `M`: Measure / Ruler tool
- `G`: Toggle Grid
- `S`: Toggle Grid Snapping
- `Space + Drag`: Pan canvas
- `Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Y`: Undo / Redo
- `Ctrl + G`: Group / Ungroup selected elements
